overview: The board conducted a focus group session regarding the Community Land Trust feasibility study and reviewed progress on the Trust Action Plan. Key discussions included the appropriation of Community Preservation Act funds and the development of a formal application process for housing developers.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Approved the minutes for the December 4, 2024, and January 8, 2025, meetings as edited.

items.title: Community Land Trust Study Focus Group
items.summary: Austin Smith of JM Goldson facilitated a discussion on the feasibility of establishing a Community Land Trust in Medford to hold land for permanent affordable housing. Trustees discussed targeting low-income elderly homeowners for anti-displacement and the importance of transit-connected family housing.

items.title: Trust Action Plan and Community Outreach
items.summary: Reviewed feedback from previous focus groups regarding housing development costs and scheduled a community workshop for March to solicit public feedback on the Trust Action Plan. The board discussed tentatively moving the workshop to March 12 to avoid a scheduling conflict with a City Council meeting on the Salem Street Corridor.

items.title: Funding for Affordable Housing
items.summary: Announced the City Council's approval of $250,000 in Community Preservation Act (CPA) funds for the trust. The board also discussed a proposal to sell city-owned parcels on McCormick Avenue to fund a Nexus study for affordable housing linkage fees, which was recently tabled by the City Council.

items.title: New Developer Inquiry and Application Process
items.summary: Discussed a funding inquiry from a non-profit developer for a 16-to-20-unit project and initiated the drafting of formal application guidelines and loan documents. Kayla Lessin volunteered to research model applications and loan terms from other municipalities to handle incoming funding requests.

items.title: Citizens' Housing and Planning Association (CHAPA) Assistance
items.summary: Reviewed technical assistance materials and promotional flyers provided by CHAPA for the trust's upcoming public outreach efforts.
